tasks.topic: A core-based parallel-flow layer model has six (thickness ft, permeability mD) pairs: L1=(8,35), L2=(12,120), L3=(15,75), L4=(9,240), L5=(20,55), L6=(6,400). These are user-supplied measurements, not literature values.
tasks.goal: Using the KB parallel-layer relation, compute total thickness, thickness-weighted effective permeability, and each layer's fraction of total kh. Rank the three largest kh contributors and explain why the thinnest layer can lead.

success_criteria.description: Use and cite the KB thickness-weighted arithmetic parallel-flow relation.
Compute total thickness and effective permeability with ft and mD units.
Report the top three kh contributors and their percentages, distinguishing user measurements from KB formula.

required_claims.text: Parallel layers share pressure drop and use thickness-weighted arithmetic permeability.
kh contribution order is L6 > L4 > L2; the thin high-k L6 can dominate.

tasks.topic: A one-dimensional core composite has six beds in series, each with equal cross-section. User measurements (length ft, k mD): B1=(6,30), B2=(14,90), B3=(18,150), B4=(9,45), B5=(22,220), B6=(11,500).
tasks.goal: Calculate the series effective permeability, the length-weighted arithmetic result someone might mistakenly apply, and the arithmetic overstatement relative to the correct series result. Identify the resistance bottleneck.

success_criteria.description: Use and cite series harmonic permeability, not parallel arithmetic weighting.
Give harmonic and arithmetic comparison values in mD.
Give overstatement percent and explain low-k bottleneck using the supplied values.

required_claims.text: Series beds share rate and add pressure loss; use a length-weighted harmonic mean.
Low permeability increases series resistance, so arithmetic weighting overstates k.

tasks.topic: At comparable stabilized conditions, five wells have user-measured (oil rate STB/day, reservoir pressure psia, flowing pressure psia): A=(420,3200,3075), B=(640,3150,2930), C=(525,3300,3130), D=(780,3400,3180), E=(610,3250,3035).
tasks.goal: Apply the KB oil productivity-index formula to all five wells. Report each J in STB/day/psi, rank by J, compare with raw-rate ranking, and explain why the top raw producer need not have the best PI.

success_criteria.description: Cite and use J=q_o/(p_e-p_w) with positive drawdown.
Calculate all five well indices in STB/day/psi.
Give correct PI and raw-rate rankings and distinguish normalization from rate.

required_claims.text: Productivity index normalizes oil rate by pressure drawdown.
PI order D>A>C>B>E differs from raw-rate order D>B>E>C>A.

tasks.topic: User-supplied metric volumetric case: reservoir area A=1,850,000 m2, net pay h=14 m, porosity phi=0.205, water saturation Sw=0.24, oil FVF Bo=1.27 reservoir m3/stock-tank m3. Independently change (i) Sw to 0.30, (ii) phi to 0.18, (iii) Bo to 1.35 while holding every other base input fixed.
tasks.goal: Use the KB STOIIP relation to calculate the base stock-tank oil volume and all three one-at-a-time sensitivities. Give each percent change from base and identify which sensitivity has the largest negative effect; avoid treating the three changes as simultaneous.

success_criteria.description: Cite and use STOIIP=A*h*phi*(1-Sw)/Bo with coherent metric units.
Report base and all three one-at-a-time volumes in stock-tank m3.
Report all three percent deltas and correctly identify the largest drop.

required_claims.text: STOIIP in stock-tank volume uses A h phi (1-Sw) divided by Bo.
Reducing porosity to 0.18 yields the largest drop among the isolated cases.

tasks.topic: Use the entire 11-point appraisal-well RFT depth/pressure table in Heriot-Watt Well Test Analysis page 81; unlike a two-zone fit, fit one ordinary-least-squares line to all listed rows. Measurements and units must come from that KB table, not from assumed user data.
tasks.goal: Give the global pressure-on-depth slope (psi/ft), root-mean-square pressure residual (psi), and the depth of the largest absolute pressure residual. Explain why the global slope/residual alone cannot establish a unique contact in the gas reservoir.

success_criteria.description: Retrieve all 11 KB RFT pairs and use one OLS pressure-on-depth fit.
Report global slope, residual RMSE, and depth of largest absolute residual with units.
Explain why one global fit does not uniquely prove fluid contact, citing the KB table/context.

required_claims.text: Use all eleven RFT observations from the appraisal-well table.
A global gradient and residual pattern do not uniquely determine the fluid-contact mechanism.

tasks.topic: Three separately mapped oil blocks have user estimates (A m2, net h m, phi, Sw, Bo reservoir m3/stock-tank m3, RF): North=(1200000,12,0.19,0.22,1.20,0.27), Central=(950000,18,0.16,0.28,1.31,0.33), South=(1420000,10,0.21,0.25,1.25,0.24). Apply the same formulas independently to each block.
tasks.goal: Calculate stock-tank oil initially in place and recoverable stock-tank oil for each block, then rank blocks by recoverable volume and sum the recoverable total. Explain why the block with largest in-place oil need not lead recoverables.

success_criteria.description: Cite KB STOIIP and reserves=STOIIP*RF relations with source/user-input distinction.
Calculate each block's stock-tank in-place and recoverable volume.
Give correct recoverable ranking, total, and recovery-factor interpretation.

required_claims.text: The recoverable volume is STOIIP multiplied by recovery factor.
Central > North > South by recoverable oil even though South has the largest STOIIP.

tasks.topic: A screening estimate gives 1,600,000 stock-tank m3 oil in place; user scenarios use recovery factors 0.26 and 0.31.
tasks.goal: Using the KB recovery-factor relation, calculate the extra recoverable stock-tank oil at RF 0.31 versus 0.26 and explain the scope of this arithmetic scenario comparison.

success_criteria.description: Cite reserves=STOIIP*RF.
Give additional recoverable oil as 80,000 stock-tank m3.
Distinguish changed assumed RF from a proven field-performance forecast.

required_claims.text: Recoverable oil equals STOIIP times recovery factor.
The result is a sensitivity to an assumed RF, not an observed forecast.

tasks.topic: Two user-reported stabilized pressure-depth intervals yield gradients 0.43 psi/ft and 0.46 psi/ft; no fluid samples, calibration file, or contact depth is supplied.
tasks.goal: Compare the two gradients by their 0.03 psi/ft difference, relate them cautiously to KB hydrostatic-gradient context, and state what cannot be inferred about contact or fluid identity.

success_criteria.description: State the 0.03 psi/ft gradient difference.
Cite hydrostatic-gradient context from the KB.
Do not assert unique fluid type or contact without more evidence.

required_claims.text: Hydrostatic gradients vary with fluid properties including salinity.
Two gradients alone do not establish a unique contact or fluid identity.

tasks.topic: A hydraulically fractured well shows a derivative segment rising one log decade vertically over two log decades of time, then a flatter derivative interval. No pressure or rate values are provided.
tasks.goal: Identify the plausible early linear-flow signature, distinguish the later horizontal derivative from it, and explain what additional reservoir context is required before uniquely assigning a model.

success_criteria.description: Recognize the half-slope derivative as compatible with linear flow.
Recognize horizontal derivative as compatible with radial flow, not linear half-slope.
Avoid uniquely asserting fracture geometry from derivative shape alone, with KB citation.

required_claims.text: A +1/2 derivative slope is a linear-flow signature.
A horizontal constant derivative is a radial-flow signature.
Derivative regime attribution needs reservoir/completion context.

tasks.topic: A new observation well in a long-produced field has a scattered wireline pressure profile across tight streaks. The pressure scatter has not been screened for supercharging. No reliable numerical pressure-depth table is supplied.
tasks.goal: State how prior production and tight-zone connectivity change pressure-profile interpretation, and describe a defensible supercharging screen before claiming a barrier or fluid contact.

success_criteria.description: Interpret produced-field profiles as dynamic rather than requiring a virgin hydrostatic line.
Explain that supercharged points require an evidence-based screen, not arbitrary deletion.
Avoid unique barrier/contact inference from this unscreened cloud and cite KB context.

required_claims.text: Produced-field wireline pressure reflects depletion and flow history.
Supercharging should be checked against permeability/geological context before discarding points.
An unscreened scattered profile alone does not prove barrier or contact.
